source_policy: Primary references support definitions and stated conditions. Scenarios and worked derivations are originally authored constructions. The supplied book matrix guides sequencing; it is not independent verification of exact-edition book coverage.
purpose: Make a p-value visible as a complete probability tail, then compare it with a threshold declared in advance.
meaning: A p-value is the probability, under a specified null model, of a result at least as extreme as the observation in the prespecified direction. Here extremeness is a larger count in twelve Bernoulli trials, so the exact p-value is an upper binomial tail.

definition.setting: A sticker supplier claims p₀=1/2. Inspect 12 independent packets and test the prespecified alternative p>1/2 using the upper binomial tail at the observed count k.

signature.p-value: Probability of this count or a larger count under p₀=1/2.

conditions: A sticker supplier claims p₀=1/2. Inspect 12 independent packets and test the prespecified alternative p>1/2 using the upper binomial tail at the observed count k.

The p-value assumes the null model and the fixed one-sided alternative; it is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true. The decision threshold is α=0.05, set before seeing the count. These constructed data do not validate a supplier.
